Change has been successfully rebased and submitted as ce8d968d60f32feb5a1001c01821faf7d0c72bbe

I think this is the only location where this function is called.
As you have replace the function code with the following inline logic, the function have no caller now. Please remove the function then.
Done
This inline hardcode might be difficult to maintain. Please replace this magic number with a declared variable for the response data size for easier maintainance.
Done

Does this `unpack()` order have any impact for the resulting data?
If so, I think putting a comment here to avoid the order changing would be nice.
Done
Declaring `constexpr size_t getCurrentUtilizationResponseSize` here would be nice.
With onImmediateSuccess reverted to call decodeGetCurrentUtilizationModeResponse in PS3, the metric no longer references the response size directly.

Please remove this function, as well in the .cpp file.
I believe that it has no caller now.

Originally I inlined the decode in onImmediateSuccess to avoid re-decoding the common response header. 
On reflection I'd rather keep decodeGetCurrentUtilizationModeResponse — it preserves the existing DecodeGetCurrentUtilizationModeResponse* unit-test coverage in test_NvidiaGpuSensorTest.cpp and keeps the byte-level decode in one named place. The cost of re-decoding the 7-byte common header at a 30-second poll cadence is negligible.

Reverted in PS3 — onImmediateSuccess calls decodeGetCurrentUtilizationModeResponse again, so the function has a caller. Function and tests kept as-is.
can we use bind_front here also?
Done
Does this have to be static?

It has to be static because the callers `onImmediateSuccess` and
`onLongRunningPayload` are static. 
That said, the body is a one-liner, so I'm happy to inline it into both callers and drop this helper entirely.
Which do you prefer?
Let it be static then.
Is there a reason we need this as a shared_ptr? Can we directly use `NvidiaGpuLongRunningCommand cmd;`?

Because the helper uses `std::enable_shared_from_this` for its asio-chain lifetime management, which requires shared_ptr ownership — a value member would make weak_from_this() empty. Happy to restructure if you'd prefer.
Can we pass `config` as rvalue reference instead of by value?

By-value is the modern sink-parameter idiom and the caller already
passes a Config{...} rvalue, so there's no perf difference vs
Config&&. Happy to switch if you prefer.
LGTM
